questions.solution:
From given equations
$4 \cos \beta=-(\cos \alpha+9 \cos \gamma)$  ...(i)
$4 \sin \beta=-(\sin \alpha+9 \sin \gamma)$  ...(ii)
Squaring both sides and adding equations (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned}
& 16\left(\cos ^2 \beta+\sin ^2 \beta\right)=\left(\cos ^2 \alpha+\sin ^2 \alpha\right)+81\left(\cos ^2 \gamma+\sin ^2 \gamma\right) \\
& +18(\cos \alpha \cdot \cos \gamma+\sin \alpha \sin \gamma) \\
& 16=1+81+18 \cos (\gamma-\alpha) \Rightarrow 9 \cos (\gamma-\alpha)=-33 \\
& \Rightarrow(-33)^2=81 \cos ^2(\gamma-\alpha)
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow 1089=81 \frac{[1+\cos (2 \gamma-2 \alpha]}{2}\Rightarrow 81 \cos (2 \gamma-2 \alpha)=2097$  ...(iii)
From given equations
$9 \cos \gamma=-(\cos \alpha+4 \cos \beta)$  ...(iv)
$9 \sin \gamma=-(\sin \alpha+4 \sin \beta)$  ...(v)
Squaring both sides and adding equations (iv) and (v)
$\begin{aligned}
& 81\left(\cos ^2 \gamma+\sin ^2 \gamma\right)=\left(\cos ^2 \alpha+\sin ^2 \alpha\right)+16 \\
& \quad \quad\left(\cos ^2 \beta+\sin ^2 \beta\right)+8(\cos \alpha \cdot \cos \beta+\sin \alpha \sin \beta) \\
& \Rightarrow 81=1+16+8 \cos (\beta-\alpha) \Rightarrow \cos (\beta-\alpha)=8 \\
& \therefore \cos (2 \beta-2 \alpha)=2 \cos ^2(\beta-\alpha)-1=127 \\
& \text { Now, } 81 \cos (2 \gamma-2 \alpha)-16 \cos (2 \beta-2 \alpha) \\
& =2097-2032=65=64+1 \\
& =8 \cos (\beta-\alpha)+1
\end{aligned}$

Given :- $\cos A \cdot \cos B \cdot \cos C=\frac{1}{5}\because \quad A+B+C=\pi \Rightarrow A+B=\pi-C\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \cos (A+B)=\cos (\pi-C) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos A \cos B-\sin A \sin B=-\cos C \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos A \cos B+\cos C=\sin A \sin B\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad 1+\frac{\cos C}{\cos A \cos B}=\tan A \tan B$

Similarly, we have,  
$\tan B \tan C=1+\frac{\cos A}{\cos B \cos C}$  ...(ii)
$\tan C \tan A=1+\frac{\cos B}{\cos C \cos A}$  ...(iii)
Adding eqn. (i), (ii) and (iii), we get
$\tan A \tan B+\tan B \tan C+\tan C \tan A=3+\frac{\cos C}{\cos A \cos B}+\frac{\cos A}{\cos B \cos C}+\frac{\cos B}{\cos C \cos A}=3+\frac{\cos ^2 C+\cos ^2 A+\cos ^2 B}{\cos A \cos B \cos C}=3+5\left(\cos ^2 C+\cos ^2 A+\cos ^2 B\right)$  ...(iv)
On $\triangle A B C$,
$\cos ^2 A+\cos ^2 B+\cos ^2 C=1-2 \cos A \cos B \cos C$ ...(v)
Using eqn. (v) in eqn. (iv), we get
$\tan A \tan B+\tan B \tan C+\tan C \tan A=3+5(1-2 \cos A \cos B \cos C)=3+5\left(1-2 \times \frac{1}{5}\right)=3+5 \times \frac{3}{5}=3+3\Rightarrow \quad \tan A \tan B+\tan B \tan C+\tan C \tan A=6$

questions.q:
If \(\alpha, \beta\) and \(\gamma\) are angles that satisfy the following conditions, find the value of \(x y z\).
1. \(\tan (\alpha)+\tan (\beta)+\tan (\gamma)\)
\(=\tan (\alpha) \cdot \tan (\beta) \cdot \tan (\gamma)\)
2. \(x=\cos (\alpha)+i \sin (\alpha)\)
3. \(y=\cos (\boldsymbol{\beta})+i \sin (\boldsymbol{\beta})\)
4. \(z=\cos (\gamma)+i \sin (\gamma)\)
questions.solution:
It is given that,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \tan \alpha+\tan \beta+\tan \gamma=\tan \alpha \tan \beta \tan \gamma \\
& \Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=-\tan \gamma(1-\tan \alpha \tan \beta) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \tan \beta}=\tan (-\gamma) \\
& \Rightarrow \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan (-\gamma) \Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=n \pi-\gamma, n \in \mathbf{I} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \alpha+\beta+\gamma=n \pi, n \in \mathbf{I} \\
& \text {and } x=\cos \alpha+i \sin \alpha, y=\cos \beta+i \sin \beta, \\
& z=\cos \gamma+i \sin \gamma \\
& \therefore \quad x y z=e^{i \alpha} . e^{i \beta} . e^{i \gamma} \\
& \quad=e^{i(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)}=e^{i n \pi}=\cos n \pi=1 \text { or }-1 \\
& \therefore \quad x y z= \pm 1
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.solution:
Given,
\(\theta=\frac{\pi}{5}=36^{\circ}\)
\(\begin{aligned} & \tan \left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)=\tan 36^{\circ}=\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}} \\ & \tan 2 \theta=\tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{5}\right)=\frac{2 \tan 36^{\circ}}{1-\tan ^2 36^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{2 \sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{1-(5-2 \sqrt{5})} \\ & =\frac{2 \sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{2 \sqrt{5}-4}=\frac{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{\sqrt{5}-2} \\ & \text {Now, } \tan \left(\frac{4 \pi}{5}\right)=\frac{2 \tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{5}\right)}{1-\tan ^2 \frac{2 \pi}{5}}=\frac{\frac{2 \cdot \sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{\sqrt{5}-2}}{1-\frac{5-2 \sqrt{5}}{(\sqrt{5}-2)^2}} \\ & \therefore \quad \cot \left(\frac{4 \pi}{5}\right)=\frac{1-\frac{5-2 \sqrt{5}}{(\sqrt{5}-2)^2}}{\frac{2 \cdot \sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{\sqrt{5}-2}} \\ & =\frac{(\sqrt{5}-2)^2-5+2 \sqrt{5}}{2(\sqrt{5}-2)(\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5})}}=\frac{5+4-4 \sqrt{5}-5+2 \sqrt{5}}{2(\sqrt{5}-2)(\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}})} \\ & =\frac{4-2 \sqrt{5}}{2(\sqrt{5}-2)(\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5})}}=\frac{(2-\sqrt{5})}{(\sqrt{5}-2)(\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}})} \\ & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\ & \end{aligned}\)
Now, \(\tan \frac{\pi}{5}+2 \tan \frac{2 \pi}{5}+4 \cot \frac{4 \pi}{5}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& =\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}+2 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{\sqrt{5}-2}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& =\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}+2 \frac{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}{\sqrt{5}-2} \times \frac{\sqrt{5}+2}{\sqrt{5}+2}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& =\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}+2\left(\sqrt{5}+2\right) \sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& =\frac{5-2 \sqrt{5}+2(\sqrt{5}+2)(5-2 \sqrt{5})-4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& \frac{=5-2 \sqrt{5}+(2 \sqrt{5}+4)(5-2 \sqrt{5})-4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& =\frac{5-2 \sqrt{5}+10 \sqrt{5}-20+20-8 \sqrt{5}-4}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}} \\
& =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5-2 \sqrt{5}}}=1 \cdot 37=\cot \frac{\pi}{5}=\cot 36^{\circ}
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: If $\sin A+\sin B+\sin C=0$ and $\cos A+\cos B+\cos C=0$, then $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)$ is equal to

Here, we have the pattern of data in $\cos x$ and $\sin x$, so let's use the method of polar form of complex number.
Polar form of complex number,
$z=\cos \theta+i \sin \theta$
then $\bar{z}=\cos \theta-i \sin \theta$
and $z \bar{z}=1\Rightarrow \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}$
Let $z_1=\cos A+i \sin Az_2=\cos B+i \sin B$
and $z_3=\cos C+i \sin C$
Then, $\quad \bar{z}_1=\cos A-i \sin A\begin{gathered}
\bar{z}_2=\cos B-i \sin B \\
z_3=\cos C-\sin C
\end{gathered}$
Now, to find $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)\begin{aligned}
& \bar{z}_1+\bar{z}_2+\bar{z}_3=(\cos A-i \sin A) \\
& +(\cos B-i \sin B)+(\cos C-i \sin C) \\
& =(\cos A+\cos B+\cos C)-i(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)=0 \\
& \frac{1}{z_1}+\frac{1}{z_2}+\frac{1}{z_3}=0 \quad\left[\because \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}\right] \\
& z_1 z_2+z_2 z_3+z_3 z_1=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A+i \sin A)(\cos B+i \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A \cos B-\sin A \sin B) \\
& +i(\sin A \cos B+\cos A \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)+i \sin (A+B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing the real part, we get
$\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)=0$
